 Order

This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to call for the entire records pursuant to the C.C.No.127 of 2022 in Crime No.14 of 2021 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate, Neyveli and quash the same in so far as the petitioners are is concerned.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that, 1st petitioner is the husband of the defacto complainant, 2nd petitioner is the mother-in-law, 3rd petitioner is the sister-in-law and 4th petitioner is the uncle of the 1st petitioner.

It is seen from the complaint and allegations made in the final report that, petitioners have committed cruelty against the defacto complainant by demanding dowry using abusive words and making physical assault.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that First Information Report in Crime No.14 of 2021 for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 294(b) and 506(i) of IPC and 4 of Tamil Nadu Dowry Prohibition Act came to be registered.
After investigation, final report was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis filed.
The case is now pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, Neyveli in C.C.No.127 of 2022.
Petitioners and 2nd respondent/defacto complainant filed Joint Memo of Compromise stating that, due to the intervention of friends and relatives, the misunderstanding between the parties is resolved.
The 1st petitioner and 2nd respondent/defacto complainant are living together with their children.
A consent affidavit is also filed in this regard.
Therefore, he seeks for quashing the C.C.No.127 of 2022 in Crime No.14 of 2021 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate, Neyveli.
3. The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) submitted that, by passage of time, the parties have decided to bury their hatchet and compromise the dispute amicably among themselves.
4. A Joint Memo of Compromise dated 12.02.2023 has been filed before this Court, which have been signed by the petitioners and the second respondent and also by the learned counsel for the parties.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
The petitioner and the second respondent were also present in person before this Court and they were identified by Ms.R.Jayanthi, S1- 08, AWPS, Neyveli.
This Court also enquired both the parties and is satisfied that the parties have come to an amicable settlement between themselves.

The second respondent answered this Court, that she had entered into a Memorandum of compromise with the petitioners and she has no objection for quashing the Charge sheet in C.C.No.127 of 2022 in Crime No.14 of 2021 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate, Neyveli.

6. Considering the fact that, the issue between the parties relates to matrimonial issue and that the second respondent does not want to prosecute the case against the petitioners and that she has no objection for quashment of proceedings and also considering that the offences are compoundable offence, no useful purpose will be served in keeping the charge sheet in C.C.No.127 of 2022 in Crime No.14 of 2021 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate, Neyveli against the petitioners.
